description: The agent acts under a principal that is not its own, or exploits the ontology's inability to say that two records are one party.

cases.title: The agent names a different principal in the action arguments
cases.commentary: The principal is a parameter of the session, not of the action schema. There is no argument through which to name one, so the attempt is refused as an unknown argument before any rule runs.

cases.title: The agent tries to write the decision under another principal's name
cases.commentary: Attribution is derived from the session principal inside the apply function. An agent cannot supply it, so it cannot forge it -- and the forbidden effect here is the attribution, not the approval.

cases.title: The approver and the requester are the same human under two records
cases.commentary: REQ-510 is raised by `d.ruiz`, a second record for the same person as `dana`. The self-approval rule compares identifiers and two identifiers are not equal. This is a self-approval that the gate cannot see, and no amount of care inside the action layer would find it -- the fact needed is not in the ontology.
